info.bio:
Social Distortion (Social D.) es una banda de rock and roll punk fundada en California en 1978.

Historia 

La banda fue formada a finales de 1978 por Mike Ness cuando era un adolescente. Tocaron con bandas como the Adolescents, China White y Shattered Faith como parte del movimiento naciente del hardcore. Su música era rápida, enojada y enérgica. En 1984 la banda apareció en el documental Another State of Mind, escrito, producido y dirigido por Peter Stuart y Adam Small (co-creador de "Mad TV").

scenes.name: Hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk como «violento, rápido y ruidoso» tarda en conquistar EE UU, pero cuando lo hace el hardcore se convierte durante dos décadas en el idioma nacional de millones de chavales. Misfits y el «scum-rock»; el crossover punk-metal (Suicidal Tendencies, Corrosion Of Conformity, Agnostic Front); Mission Of Burma en Boston. Washington: Bad Brains (reggae, funk y metal diez años por delante), Minor Threat (el «straight-edge») y Rites Of Spring, inventores del emo-core. San Francisco: Dead Kennedys de Jello Biafra, D.R.I. (thrash antes que Metallica), Flipper. Los «beach punks» de Los Ángeles: Germs, X, Black Flag (Damaged), Descendents, Gun Club (Fire Of Love), Bad Religion. El jazz-core de Minutemen y Saccharine Trust; en el Medio Oeste, Husker Du y Replacements cambian el hardcore para siempre; en Chicago, Naked Raygun y Big Black de Steve Albini; en Europa, The Ex y los italianos CCCP.

podcast.title: Cuckoo's Nest Performances
podcast.body: Social Distortion was among the punk bands that performed at The Cuckoo's Nest in Costa Mesa, a club renowned for its role in the early development of slam dancing. "The place hosted a lot of punk shows, from the Ramones to the Dam to Social Distortion."

podcast.title: Heroin Problem Overcome
podcast.body: Mike Ness of Social Distortion successfully overcame a heroin addiction. "Mike Ness of Social Distortion had a heroin problem that he managed to kick and Shannon Hoon of Blind Mel and had a drug counselor but he wasn't able to keep Hoon from OD and dying."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Major Artists
podcast.body: Social Distortion is cited among several California hardcore bands that were very important to the musical education of figures like Eddie Vedder and Dave Grohl. "Talk to Eddie Vetter or Dave Grohl, and they'll tell you how some of these bands were really, really important to their musical education."

podcast.title: Long-running Career and Struggles
podcast.body: Social Distortion had been actively performing since 1978, often without significant mainstream success. Their leader, Mike Ness, was known for being unpredictable and prone to selling band equipment to fund drug use. "Social distortion had been plugging away without a whole lot of success since 1978. Leader Mike Ness was unpredictable and prone to hawking the band equipment for drugs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Major Label Success with Savvy Management
podcast.body: After acquiring astute management, Social Distortion stabilized, signed with a major label, and began producing alt-rock radio hits. Their management team was the same as The Offspring's, which allowed Social Distortion to benefit from The Offspring's surge in popularity. "But after finally acquiring some savvy management, social defund their footing, signed to a major label and started putting out alt-rock radio hits like this. By the way, they were managed by the same people as the offspring, so when that group took off, Social D was cut and they're up-trapped, much to their benefit of course."

xref.title: Music as Escape and Teenage Influences
xref.body: Following a football injury that sidelined him for much of a season, music became Scott Weiland's primary escape. His favorite bands during this period included Depeche Mode, The Clash, Social Distortion, The Sweet, Echo & The Bunnymen, and Queen. "Music became his escape, especially after a football injury forced him to sit out much of a season."

xref.title: Third Wave Pioneers
xref.body: Formed in 1983 in Boston, The Mighty Mighty Bosstones were early practitioners of the third wave of Ska, initially inspired by the Two Tone movement but also incorporating hard rock influences from bands like ACDC, Motorhead, and Social Distortion. They became prominent in the late 1980s and early 1990s by fusing Ska with hardcore elements. "The Mighty Mighty Boss Tones. They were formed in 1983 and inspired by the whole two-tone thing, at least originally."
